title: Release channel safety-net and cross-surface compatibility map
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and deliver a friction-minimizing LTS-like channel model across runtime, REST API, SDKs, and Console. Provide a single compatibility map and a safety-net rollout choreography that enables automated checks, staged rollouts, and predictable upgrade windows for customers using hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
background: Multiple teams have independently handled compatibility and rollouts for their surface (runtime, API, SDK, console). This has led to mismatched expectations during upgrades: console features assume API stability that the runtime ABI didn't guarantee, SDKs bump dependency versions unexpectedly, and Dedicated customers hit upgrade windows without automated fallbacks. We need a unified compatibility artefact + operational gates to reduce customer breakage and shorten incident MTTI.
goals: Define cross-surface compatibility rules (minor/patch safe, major with migration) and a machine-readable compatibility map
Create rollout gates (canary, progressive percentage, buffer window, auto-fallback) and embed them into deployment pipelines
Ship an upgrade assistant (compat-ci) that runs compatibility checks for PRs across runtime, API, SDKs, and Console
Document supported upgrade paths and a 12-month support cadence for stable channels with clear deprecation windows
non_goals: Redesign of runtime internals unrelated to public API/ABI guarantees
Changing billing or pricing model as part of this work
proposed_solution: Publish a versioned compatibility manifest format (YAML/JSON) that each surface produces on release. The manifest declares compatibility stamps: api-contract, runtime-abi, sdk-major, console-schema. CI will run 'compat-ci' that validates new manifests against active channel rules. Releases are gated with an automated choreography: preflight validation -> canary (1%) -> progressive (10/30/60) with guardrails; failures trigger automated fallback to the previous pinned compatible model variant. Dedicated/Private customers get a scheduled opt-in window and an 'upgrade-safe' toggle in the Console.
compatibility_matrix_summary: Map rows: runtime binary ABI, REST API (v*), SDKs (language + minor), Console JSON schema. Columns: supported channel (stable, extended, experimental), guaranteed compatibility (yes/limited/no), recommended migration path. Key rules: patch releases must be no-op for public contracts; minor releases may add opt-in features behind flags; major releases require compat manifest + migration guide and a 6-week staged rollout window.
rollout_gates: Preflight CI: manifest validation, integration smoke tests, migration checklists
Gate 0: internal canary in staging clusters for 48h
Gate 1: 1% production canary for 24h with automated anomaly detection (latency/error/cost)
Gate 2: progressive ramp (10%, 30%, 60%) with 24h hold at each step
Gate 3: global rollout with 72h monitoring baseline and automatic rollback rule
upgrade_tooling_requirements: compat-ci: GitHub action that validates manifests and runs cross-surface smoke tests
manifest-linter: enforces stamps and deprecation metadata
console-upgrade-panel: UI to schedule upgrades, show blockers, and toggle 'upgrade-safe'
rollback-operator: runbook automation to revert routing and model pins in <5 minutes
migration_strategy: For each major incompatibility we produce: migration guide, code snippets for SDK changes, a compatibility shim when feasible, and sample transformation scripts for persisted KV cache migrations. For Dedicated/Private, we offer a staged contractor-run upgrade and a 'pause-upgrades' flag customers can set during critical periods.
monitoring_and_telemetry: SLO guardrails: token-latency, tail-latency P99, error-rate thresholds
Automated regression alerts tied to the release manifest and visible in Console
Post-release audit: list of customers upgraded, rollback events, and incident tickets
open_risks: Runtime ABI introspection is incomplete — risk of silent incompatibility
Customers on pinned private deployments may skip safety gates and require manual coordination
Cross-surface test matrix growth (combinatorial explosion) — may slow down CI
notes: We will align channel names with marketing (stable/extended/experimental) but maintain strict internal semantics for compatibility guarantees.
Consider a backward-compatibility badge that surfaces in SDK releases and Console release notes.
Propose a dedicated 2-week stabilization window before major runtime releases are shipped to stable channel customers.
updates: 2026-03-11: Initial spike completed. Prototype manifest schema created and validated against runtime-2.0 alpha.
2026-03-12: compat-ci PoC runs on SDK repo; found 3 minor contract breakages (PRs linked).
2026-03-13: Aligned rollout gates with SRE. Security review requested; planning meeting scheduled 2026-03-16.
